title: The canonical matching module and its normalized chart equations
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\mathcal U$ be a universe-small locally directed open cover of $X$ with index category $I$, and give modules $M_i$ on its members with tensor-pullback transition isomorphisms $t_f$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Put $P_i=(\mathcal U_i\to X)_*M_i$. For $f:i\to j$, define $r_f:P_j\to P_i$ by taking the normalized adjoint of $t_f$, applying pushforward, and transporting along the specified equality of the composite map to $X$. Choose one arrow for each pair $(i,j)$ with an inhabited hom $i\to j$. The matching module $L$ is the multiequalizer of the maps $\mathrm{id}:P_i\to P_i$ and the chosen $r_f:P_j\to P_i$. Index relations by pairs $(i,j)$ with an inhabited hom $i\to j$; thus the limit index remains in universe $u$. Its projections have adjoints $c_i:(\mathcal U_i\to X)^*L\to M_i$. If $I$ is thin, these maps satisfy precisely the normalized tensor-pullback chart equation, including its equality transport. These are explicit limit constructions and require no cocycle for their definition.

proof.text: Construct r_f by the normalized hom equivalence and canonical pushforward composition. Uniqueness of left adjoints and the composed adjunction identify the mate of the normalized pullback comparison with the composite pushforward transition. Equality transports are retained explicitly.

Form the universe-small multicospan with one left object P_i per chart and one right object P_i for each inhabited hom i→j, with incoming maps identity and r_f. Take its multiequalizer in X.Modules; all limits used exist in Mathlib. Projection adjoints define the canonical chart maps.

The universal multiequalizer relation gives projection(j)≫r_f=projection(i). Thinness equates the selected arrow to the supplied arrow. Apply the normalized adjunction and the mate formula to obtain the exact eqToHom/normalized-composition chart equation. No local invertibility assertion is used.
